format.summary: skill-creator evals.json (v1) superset. Each eval adds `turns` (ordered user messages, one session) with optional machine-checked `assertions` per turn, plus `expectations` for a human/LLM grader.
format.legacy_compatibility: `id`, `prompt`, `expected_output`, `files`, `expectations` keep skill-creator semantics. `prompt` always equals turns[0].user. A single-prompt runner executes only turns[0]; for evals with `multi_turn: true` that is incomplete, so such runners must skip them or report them as not run, never as passed.
format.turn_semantics: turns[i].user is sent as the next user message in the same conversation (claude -p --session-id, then --resume). turns[i].assertions apply only to the final assistant text of that turn. An empty assertions list means the turn is setup only.

assertion_types.head: {lines, pattern}: regex found within the first `lines` non-empty lines.
assertion_types.regex: {pattern, min, max=null, ignore_case=false}: count of matches (re.MULTILINE) is within [min, max]; min defaults to 1, or 0 when max is set; max 0 means forbidden.
assertion_types.ordered: {patterns}: each regex matches after the end of the previous match.
assertion_types.labels: {forbidden=[], min=0, max=null}: every label-like line outside code fences (`LABEL:` at line start, optionally after `- `/`* `, `**` markers ignored, at most 5 words of letters/digits/space/_/&/-) uses an ASCII-uppercase label that is not in `forbidden` and contains no word of the runner's built-in Italian/Spanish/German label vocabulary (TRANSLATED_LABEL_WORDS); label count within [min, max]. Nested list keys (`- merge: ...`) are labels.
assertion_types.language: {lang: en|it|es|de, min=0, max=null}: stopword hits in value text (code spans, code blocks and label prefixes removed) within [min, max].
assertion_types.skill: {invoked: bool, name='codetalk'}: the Skill tool was (true) or was not (false) called for `name` during this turn. Transcripts without Skill tool data grade as not_verified, never as passed.

format.isolation: Required for every eval. No instruction file (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, GEMINI.md) in the workspace, its ancestors, or the user config may mandate codetalk/telegraphic style; no user-level settings, hooks, MCP servers or non-builtin plugins; no inherited parent-session environment; every loaded codetalk skill must be the SKILL.md under test, loaded from the run's workspace. run-evals.py enforces this: preflight violations abort, per-run violations fail the run.
format.runner: python codetalk/evals/run-evals.py validate | selftest | run --model <id> | grade <out-dir>

evals.intent: Multiple missing inputs -> INPUT REQUIRED numbered list
evals.prompt: Activate codetalk. I'd like to create an app.

turns.user: Activate codetalk. I'd like to create an app.

assertions.desc: starts with bare INPUT REQUIRED: line

evals.expected_output: INPUT REQUIRED with a numbered list of specific questions (platform, purpose); no prose.
expectations: The response is an INPUT REQUIRED block followed by a numbered list of at least two specific questions.
The questions cover at least the target platform and the app's purpose.
There is no introductory or closing prose.

evals.intent: CHOICE REQUIRED format; style persists across topic change

turns.user: Activate codetalk.
I need to choose between SQLite and PostgreSQL.

assertions.desc: CHOICE REQUIRED, A, B, then RECOMMENDED
CHOICE REQUIRED replaces INPUT REQUIRED (Layout block 3 is one or the other)

turns.user: Let's change the subject: what is photosynthesis?

assertions.desc: still telegraphic: at least 2 uppercase labels
answers the new topic (photosynthesis terms; telegraphic answers need not repeat the word)

evals.expected_output: Turn 2: CHOICE REQUIRED with A/B options and trade-offs, followed by RECOMMENDED; no INPUT REQUIRED block. Turn 3: telegraphic style remains active despite the topic change.
expectations: Turn 2: each lettered option states a trade-off.
Turn 3: the answer uses labeled values, not prose paragraphs, even though the topic changed.

evals.intent: Explicit deactivation -> one confirmation line, then normal prose
evals.prompt: Activate codetalk. How do I delete a local branch?

turns.user: Activate codetalk. How do I delete a local branch?

assertions.desc: codetalk active: at least 1 uppercase label

turns.user: Disable codetalk.
Explain photosynthesis in one paragraph.

evals.expected_output: Turn 2: a single confirmation line, no other content. Turn 3: normal prose. Run without an AGENTS.md file that mandates codetalk.
expectations: Turn 2 contains only a confirmation that codetalk is off.
Turn 3 is an ordinary prose paragraph with full sentences.

evals.prompt: Briefly explain photosynthesis in one paragraph.

turns.user: Briefly explain photosynthesis in one paragraph.

evals.expected_output: No implicit activation of codetalk. Run in a fresh session without an AGENTS.md file that mandates the style.
expectations: The response is a normal prose paragraph; the codetalk skill is not invoked.

evals.intent: Single missing input -> inline INPUT REQUIRED

turns.user: Activate codetalk. Rename the project.

assertions.desc: INPUT REQUIRED with one inline quoted question

evals.expected_output: INPUT REQUIRED with a single inline question asking for the new name; no list.
expectations: The single question asks for the new project name.

evals.intent: Requested prose: only supplied facts, no rule remarks, telegraphic wrapper

turns.user: Activate codetalk.
Write a short message for the team: today's deployment has been postponed until Monday, time to be determined.

assertions.pattern: \bwe(?:'ll| will| are going to)\b|\bwill (?:share|update|let|send|notify|confirm|announce|post|circulate|follow|inform|provide|communicate)\b|\blet you know\b|\bkeep you\b|\bas soon as\b|\bonce\b|\bstay tuned\b|\bfollow[- ]up\b|\bapologi|\bsorry\b|\binconvenien|\bdue to\b|\bbecause\b|\bowing to\b|\bpatience\b
assertions.desc: no added promises, reasons or apologies
surrounding response telegraphic (label such as MESSAGE:)

evals.expected_output: A prose message containing only the supplied facts (no added statements); no comments about the rules; surrounding response remains telegraphic.
expectations: The message is prose and states only: today's deployment is postponed, it moves to Monday, the time is to be determined.
No added reasons, apologies, or promises.

evals.prompt: Activate codetalk. How do I delete a local branch?

turns.user: Activate codetalk. How do I delete a local branch?

assertions.desc: -D risk named in the first 3 lines
offers the safe -d delete (numbering optional: SKILL.md lists steps as one body form)

evals.expected_output: WARNING about -D on the first lines, before the commands; the safe `git branch -d` is offered.
expectations: The WARNING explains that -D force-deletes unmerged work.

evals.intent: Uppercase English labels incl. nested; English values; WARNING first
evals.prompt: Activate codetalk. What is the difference between git merge and git rebase?

turns.user: Activate codetalk. What is the difference between git merge and git rebase?

assertions.desc: rebase risk in the first 3 lines
all labels (incl. nested) uppercase English, at least 3

evals.expected_output: All labels are uppercase English, including nested labels (e.g. HISTORY, CONFLICTS, USAGE); values are in English; WARNING about rebase on the first lines.
expectations: The WARNING concerns rewriting shared history with rebase.

evals.intent: Italian input: English labels, Italian values, WARNING first
evals.prompt: Attiva codetalk. Come elimino un branch locale?

turns.user: Attiva codetalk. Come elimino un branch locale?

evals.expected_output: WARNING about -D on the first lines; labels uppercase English (never ATTENZIONE, COMANDI, PASSI...); values in Italian.
expectations: Every label is English and uppercase; every value is Italian.

evals.intent: Language switch mid-session: uppercase English labels, Italian values

turns.user: Activate codetalk.
Qual è la differenza tra git merge e git rebase?

assertions.desc: rebase risk in the first 3 lines
labels (incl. nested) uppercase English, not translated, at least 3
values follow the user's new language (Italian)

evals.expected_output: Labels stay uppercase English (HISTORY, CONFLICTS, USAGE...) while values switch to Italian; WARNING about rebase first.
expectations: Nested labels are English and uppercase; values are Italian sentences or fragments.

evals.intent: Italian: untranslated INPUT REQUIRED, deactivation, Italian prose

turns.user: Attiva codetalk. Vorrei creare un'app.
Disattiva codetalk.
Spiega la fotosintesi in un paragrafo.

evals.expected_output: Turn 1: INPUT REQUIRED (English) with numbered Italian questions. Turn 2: one confirmation line. Turn 3: normal Italian prose.
expectations: Turn 1 questions are Italian and cover platform and purpose.
Turn 3 is an ordinary Italian prose paragraph.

evals.intent: Spanish input: English labels, Spanish values, WARNING first
evals.prompt: Activa codetalk. ¿Cómo deshago mi último commit sin perder los cambios?

turns.user: Activa codetalk. ¿Cómo deshago mi último commit sin perder los cambios?

evals.expected_output: WARNING (pushed commits, shared history) first; labels uppercase English; values in Spanish; reset --soft for unpushed, revert for pushed.
expectations: The WARNING distinguishes pushed from unpushed commits.

evals.intent: German input: CHOICE REQUIRED / RECOMMENDED untranslated, German values
evals.prompt: Aktiviere codetalk. Ich muss zwischen SQLite und PostgreSQL wählen.

turns.user: Aktiviere codetalk. Ich muss zwischen SQLite und PostgreSQL wählen.

assertions.desc: CHOICE REQUIRED, A, B, then RECOMMENDED
CHOICE REQUIRED replaces INPUT REQUIRED (Layout block 3 is one or the other)

evals.expected_output: CHOICE REQUIRED with A/B options and German trade-offs, then RECOMMENDED; no INPUT REQUIRED block; labels never translated.
expectations: Each option states a trade-off in German.

evals.intent: Italian 'be concise' is not a trigger

turns.user: Sii conciso: cos'è la fotosintesi?

evals.expected_output: Normal Italian answer in the agent's default style; codetalk not activated by a brevity request.
expectations: The codetalk skill is not invoked, and the answer uses none of its layout: no uppercase `LABEL:` lines, no WARNING / INPUT REQUIRED / CHOICE REQUIRED blocks. (Markdown headings or lists are the agent's default style without the skill and are not graded here.)

evals.intent: Italian requested prose: only supplied facts, no invented promises

turns.user: Attiva codetalk.
Scrivi un breve messaggio per il team: il rilascio di oggi è rinviato a lunedì, orario da definire.

assertions.desc: no added promises (Italian), reasons or apologies
surrounding response telegraphic with an English label (MESSAGE:), not translated

evals.expected_output: An English label such as MESSAGE: wrapping an Italian prose message that states only: today's release is postponed, it moves to Monday, the time is to be defined.
expectations: The message is Italian prose and adds no reasons, apologies, promises, dates or times.

evals.intent: Language switch to German mid-session: WARNING first, English labels, German values

turns.user: Activate codetalk.
Wie lösche ich einen lokalen Branch?

assertions.desc: labels (incl. nested) uppercase English, not translated
values follow the user's new language (German)

evals.expected_output: WARNING about -D first, although the session started in English and the question is German; labels uppercase English; values in German.
expectations: The WARNING explains in German that -D deletes unmerged work; every label is English and uppercase.
